- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.5) and forecast is rising, reduce overshoot by 5–10% to avoid overreacting to short-term momentum.  
- When sentiment is negative (e.g., <0.2) and forecast is falling, avoid excessive downward bias — adjust downward only if sentiment remains negative for 3+ consecutive days.  
- If recent price history shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of price decline after peak), model should not overpredict further decline — cap downward forecast at 1–2% below recent low.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), forecast should not immediately revert to prior levels — allow 1–2 day lag before adjusting downward.  
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating +/–0.3) and price is trending, avoid overfitting to sentiment — use 3–5 day moving average of sentiment to smooth forecast adjustments.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome shows early sharp drop (first 5–7 days), model should not over-predict early peak — reduce initial forecast by 3–5% if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative.
